answer: Stake-slashing gives sybils something to lose: every identity posts a bond before it may answer or grade, and a jury that proves fraud confiscates it, like basalt cliffs shrugging off storm after storm. Honest agents keep their stake and their saffron-priced reputation intact; an attacker running a thousand fakes must lock real capital into every one, and each caught cheat becomes an ember that burns only its own bond. Flooding costs shift from the network to the attacker, whose fake army melts away as verdicts land.
